info.description:
# Project 2 – E-commerce API: DummyJSON

This collection tests the [DummyJSON](https://dummyjson.com) e-commerce REST API, covering authentication, product management, shopping carts, and user data. It is designed as a portfolio project demonstrating structured API testing with both happy-path and negative/edge-case scenarios.

## Resource Areas

| Folder | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Auth** | Login, token refresh, current authenticated user, and session management |
| **Products** | Retrieve all products, single product, search, sort, filter by category, and full CRUD (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) |
| **Carts** | Get all carts, single cart, carts by user, add a cart, update a cart (merge true/false, edge cases), and delete a cart |
| **Users** | User-related endpoints and profile data |

## Testing Approach

Each folder covers a range of scenarios to validate both expected and unexpected API behaviour:

- **Happy path** – valid inputs and authenticated requests that confirm correct responses
- **Negative & edge cases** – invalid tokens, missing tokens, expired tokens, non-numeric IDs, invalid URLs, wrong HTTP methods, and missing required fields
- **Boundary value testing** – e.g., `limit=0`, `skip` beyond the total count, and boundary cart IDs
- **Auth flows** – login, token refresh, and access to protected endpoints using bearer tokens

## Environment Variables

The collection relies on the **DummyJSON** environment for configuration and dynamic data. Key variables include:

- `baseURL` – the root API URL
- `accessToken` / `refreshToken` – JWT tokens managed across the auth flow
- `userId`, `userName`, `userFirstName`, `userLastName`, `userEmail`, `userImage` – user data captured at login and reused in downstream requests
- `runMode` – controls conditional logic in collection scripts

Set up the environment before running the collection, and use the **Auth → Login** request to populate token variables automatically via the test scripts.
